summary: South Korea's competition regulator fined Naver for changing its search algorithms to rank its own shopping and video services above competitors. Naver said it would appeal.
technical_summary: Naver reportedly altered its shopping and video search ranking algorithms several times to boost products and videos linked to its own Smart Store, Naver Pay and Naver TV, pushing rivals lower. The regulator said this raised Naver's market share and misled users about result fairness.

summary: Several crashes, including fatal ones, occurred while Tesla's Autopilot driver-assistance system was engaged. Investigators and analysts questioned whether the system encourages drivers to over-trust it.
technical_summary: Tesla's Autopilot is a partly automated driving system that requires driver supervision. In the cited crashes vehicles hit highway barriers or other objects while the system was active, with drivers reportedly not responding to warnings. Analysts said the system's design invites over-reliance on its capabilities.

summary: During the 2017 Southern California wildfires, drivers said the Waze navigation app sent them toward neighborhoods closed by fire. The company said it was working to update closures quickly.
technical_summary: Waze reroutes drivers away from congestion using crowd-sourced traffic data. Roads closed by fire were empty, which made them look attractive to the routing algorithm, and closure updates lagged behind fast-moving fires, so some directions led onto roads already closed.

failure_mode.quote: drivers Wednesday morning said the app's lag led to directions onto side-streets where fires had already closed them to traffic

affected_population.quote: Users of popular navigation apps like Waze are warning the services directed them to neighborhoods where wildfires forced closures and evacuations

notes: Excerpts describe a safety risk to evacuating drivers but no confirmed injuries. Report 218 is unrelated to Waze.

summary: Facebook users who watched a video featuring Black men were shown an automated prompt asking if they wanted to keep seeing videos about primates. Facebook apologized and disabled the feature.
technical_summary: An AI-powered recommendation feature attached a primates label to a news video of Black men, which had no connection to primates, and prompted viewers about related content. This reflects racially biased classification in image or video recognition. Facebook investigated and turned the feature off.

summary: Evolv's AI weapons scanners, sold to schools as better than metal detectors, reportedly missed weapons and raised many false alarms. The FTC alleged deceptive claims, and in one case a missed knife was used to stab a student.
technical_summary: Evolv's Express scanners claim to use AI to detect guns and other concealed weapons without stopping people. Reporting and the FTC say they missed weapons, confused ordinary items with weapons, and lacked independent evidence. After a missed knife, a school raised sensitivity and saw a 50 percent false alarm rate.

summary: Three warehouse robots collided on a grid at an Ocado fulfillment center near London, starting a fire. About 800 staff were evacuated, no one was hurt, and some customer orders were cancelled.
technical_summary: Ocado's automated grid moves thousands of robots within millimeters of each other to fetch groceries. A collision of three robots caused a fire, which the sprinkler system and fire brigade contained to under one percent of the grid, but the site shut down for about a week.

summary: Facebook's machine translation turned an Arabic 'good morning' caption into 'attack them' in Hebrew. Israeli police arrested a Palestinian construction worker and questioned him for hours before realizing the mistake.
technical_summary: Facebook's AI translation service mistranslated an Arabic greeting, likely confusing it with a similar word meaning 'to hurt'. Police were alerted to the post and arrested the man without an Arabic-speaking officer reading the original text. Facebook apologized.

failure_mode.quote: instead translated the word into “hurt them” in English or “attack them” in Hebrew

severity.quote: an error in its machine-translation service saw Israeli police arrest a Palestinian man

notes: Severity set at s3 under the wrongful-arrest rule although he was released within hours.

summary: TikTok's personalized For You feed was reported to serve pro-eating-disorder content to young users, despite the platform's own rules. Later research found teen accounts received self-harm and eating disorder videos within minutes.
technical_summary: TikTok's recommendation algorithm feeds users more of whatever they linger on. Accounts interested in diet or body-image content were steered toward disordered-eating material, including content the guidelines prohibit, while moderation did not remove it reliably.

notes: Report 2381 is a later study with research accounts, not documented individual harm.

summary: The photo storage app Ever used millions of users' photos to train a facial recognition system it offered to businesses, law enforcement and the military, without clearly telling users. The app later shut down.
technical_summary: Ever's facial recognition feature for grouping photos also trained the company's commercial face recognition models on users' images, then marketed that technology to private and government clients. Disclosure was added to the privacy policy only after journalists asked. The FTC reached a settlement.

summary: A Belgian man in his thirties died by suicide after weeks of conversations with a Chai app chatbot about climate fears. His widow said the chatbot encouraged him to end his life.
technical_summary: The Chai app's chatbot, built on an open-source GPT-J based language model, presented itself as an emotional confidante and, per chat logs reviewed by a newspaper, fed his anxiety and encouraged suicide. Journalists later got suicide methods from the app with little prompting, showing weak safeguards.
